segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Ten. Bisect a given segment. Given segment A B, we are to bisect it.

subsegments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Ten. Bisect a given segment. Given segment A B, we are to bisect it.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: On segment A B, construct the equilateral triangle A B C. Next, bisect angle A C B by segment C D, meeting segment A B at point D.

subsegments.text: On segment A B, construct the equilateral triangle A B C. Next, bisect angle A C B by segment C D, meeting segment A B at point D.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: In triangles A C D and B C D, side A C equals side B C, side C D is common, and the included angle A C D equals angle B C D. By Side-Angle-Side congruence, the base A D equals the base B D. Therefore segment A B has been bisected at point D, as was required to do.
